newsitem.title: USA: Emerging market debt thinly mixed in light trading.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debt thinly mixed in light trading.

text.p: Emerging market debt ended narrowly mixed in quiet trading Wednesday and spreads over Treasuries generally widened, market experts said.
"Most of the action has been in the new issues," said Raul Elizalde, head of quantitative analysis at ING Barings.
"The tone of the market over the past few weeks has been not a lot of interest in seasoned issues, including Bradies," Elizalde continued. "But there has been a lot interest in new securities."
Among major Latin American Bradies, Brazil "C" bonds were off 1/8 at 79-3/4 bid, Argentina FRBs were up 1/8 at 94 bid and Mexico pars were up 1/8 at 76-5/8 bid.

Ecuador debt gave back much of Tuesday's gains as investors paused to realize profits, traders said. The country's Brady bonds had rallied in the previous session on technicals and rumors of an upcoming buyback, they said.
Late Wednesday, Ecuador PDIs were off 5/8 at 66-5/8, while discounts were off 7/8 at 72-5/8.
"Buyback rumors got people a little excited, and then we just erased some of those gains today," one trader said.

Ecuador said Wednesday it plans to announce three fiscal austerity measures by week's end, including a new tax scheme for fuel distributors, lower electricity tariffs and the collection of debt from electricity firm Emelec.
Some U.S.-based analysts said they were skeptical about how much the fiscal plan could reduce Ecuador's budget deficit.

Buyback talk once again swirled around Venezuela debt, but investors largely disregarded it, players said. The discussion stemmed from a report in newspaper El Nacional outlining possibilities for a repurchase program, they said.
Venezuela FLIRBs were up 1/8 at 92-3/8 bid and discounts held steady at 87-5/8.
"A lot of the buyback rumors were priced in last week," another Brady trader said. "Venezuela pretty much gave back all of its gains yesterday."
More broadly, Argentina's global 2017 was up 1/8 at 109-7/8 bid, Bulgaria IABs rose 3/8 to 69-1/4 and dollar-denominated Russian Vnesh loans slipped 1/8 to 89-1/4.
